reports.title: Identification of Urinary Biomarkers for Exercise-Induced Immunosuppression by iTRAQ Proteomics
reports.authors: Xu G; Lin W; McAinch AJ; Yan X; Weng X
source_locator: p.1 header: 'Received 24 September 2019; Revised 20 November 2019; Accepted 30 December 2019; Published 25 January 2020'
reports.reviewer_notes: provisional FT code: FT04_NO_QUALIFYING_EXERCISE_EXPOSURE. Design is a 4-week progressive INCREMENTAL TRAINING programme (5 d/week, intensity stepped 60/70/80/90% VO2max by week), sampled once per week (fasting blood+urine, Sunday 07:00) plus a pre-training baseline (UW0/W0); it is not an identifiable single acute bout with a stated exercise-end-to-sample interval, and it is not Support B (no >=2 discretely identified bouts with documented bout-to-sample timing; 'end of training week' is a cumulative multi-session block, not one identified bout). Matches FT04 example 'training pre/post comparison with no recoverable acute bout or post-exercise sampling relation'. Provisionally retained as background (training-adaptation/immunosuppression monitoring) per pilot_purpose instruction to apply v2 background rules pending team adjudication; this is the exact boundary case the pilot purpose flags for R42. Locator: p.2 Methods 2.2-2.3 (Figure 1 weekly training blocks; sample collection 'at the end of each training week ... on each Sunday morning').
reports.author_stated_use: 'Four proteins in the urine, SEMG-1, PIP, PDGFRL, and NDPK, ... have the potential to be used as noninvasive immune biomarkers of exercise-induced immunosuppression.' (Abstract/Conclusion, p.1 & p.10)
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.2 Introduction: 'the period of immunosuppression after high-intensity exercise is called the 'open window' period [18]'

sample_sets.sample_notes: ELISA validation of SEMG-1, PIP, PDGFRL, NDPK (Table 7). Table 7 reports mean +/- SD across what appears to be n=15 individuals with one-way ANOVA (2.11), which implies INDIVIDUAL (non-pooled) urine samples for this validation step -- in contrast to the POOLED iTRAQ discovery-phase samples (see SS-R42-11..15). However, Methods 2.10 does not explicitly state whether ELISA used pooled or individual urine; this is inferred, not stated, and is flagged as an unresolved question. Confirmed: the ELISA-validated cohort is the SAME 15 participants as the iTRAQ discovery phase (no independent/second cohort is described anywhere in the paper) -- i.e. 'validation' here is same-cohort orthogonal-assay confirmation, not an independent validation cohort.

sample_sets.sample_notes: ELISA validation of SEMG-1, PIP, PDGFRL, NDPK (Table 7). Table 7 reports mean +/- SD across what appears to be n=15 individuals with one-way ANOVA (2.11), which implies INDIVIDUAL (non-pooled) urine samples for this validation step -- in contrast to the POOLED iTRAQ discovery-phase samples (see SS-R42-11..15). However, Methods 2.10 does not explicitly state whether ELISA used pooled or individual urine; this is inferred, not stated, and is flagged as an unresolved question. Confirmed: the ELISA-validated cohort is the SAME 15 participants as the iTRAQ discovery phase (no independent/second cohort is described anywhere in the paper) -- i.e. 'validation' here is same-cohort orthogonal-assay confirmation, not an independent validation cohort.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: The exposure is a 4-week progressive incremental-intensity training programme sampled once weekly (fasting blood+urine, Sunday 07:00) with no stated exercise-end-to-sample interval (p.2 Methods 2.2-2.3, Fig. 1), so neither Core A (identifiable single bout with a known post-cessation sampling time) nor Support B (>=2 discretely identified bouts with documented bout-to-sample timing) is clearly satisfied; this matches FT04's 'training pre/post comparison with no recoverable acute bout or post-exercise sampling relation' example. Provisionally retained as background training/immunosuppression-monitoring evidence per v2 rules, as instructed by the pilot_purpose for this report; final disposition needs team adjudication of whether the fixed weekly training-to-Sunday-draw schedule counts as sufficiently 'known timing' for Support B.

unresolved_questions: Is the fixed training-week-to-Sunday-sample schedule (Fig. 1) sufficiently well-defined timing to qualify this as Support B (repeated identified bouts with known bout-to-sample timing), or does it remain background/FT04 because the 'bout' is a 5-session weekly block rather than one identified session? This is the core calibration question flagged by pilot_purpose for R42.

Methods 2.10 does not state whether the ELISA validation of SEMG1/PIP/PDGFRL/NDPK (Table 7) used pooled or individual urine; the mean+/-SD + one-way-ANOVA presentation suggests individual-level sampling, in contrast to the explicitly POOLED iTRAQ discovery samples (Methods 2.7: 'combined into one urine sample for each time point'), but this is inferred, not stated. Recorded as UNCLEAR in sample_sets.matrix/n_biological_samples for SS-R42-16..20.

Row-unit choice for Tables 5-7: each co-differential/validated protein was charted as ONE measurement row spanning all 4 weekly fold-change/concentration values (rather than 4 separate per-week-comparison rows). Manual's 'per named candidate x comparison' row unit is ambiguous for this kind of multi-timepoint table; flag for team decision on the standard convention.

cohorts.adult_stratum_separable: only mean+/-SD age (19.2+/-0.7 y) is given for the 15 male students, with no explicit inclusion age criterion or range; marked UNCLEAR rather than all_participants_adult, since the strict rule is not to infer.

Whether the GO-annotated 'immune system process' proteins (Fig. 4, 10 of the 24 co-differential proteins) should be separately tagged as the manual's 'named immune candidate' subset (aims/methods-linked), given the paper's stated aim is explicitly immune-biomarker discovery even though protein selection itself was an unbiased fold-change/co-expression screen, not an a priori immune-target list.

marker_family vocabulary: urinary immunoglobulin fragments (IGKC, IGLV3-21, IGLV4-69, IGLV2-18) and complement factor CD55 (Table 6) arguably fit 'immunoglobulin_or_complement' rather than 'proteome'; charted here as 'proteome' (omics-platform-based) for internal consistency with the other 23 iTRAQ-discovered proteins, but this is a judgment call worth standardising.
